newsitem.title: USA: US spot gas prices edge higher on brief cold snap.
newsitem.headline: US spot gas prices edge higher on brief cold snap.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices edged higher Wednesday as the Northeast awaited colder weather Thursday and early next week, sources said.
Swing Gulf Coast pipes rose by more than five cents to the mid-$2.30s to low-$2.40s.
"Prices are up on this cold coming in, but with not much weather behind it and plenty of storage, prices probably won't move any higher," one trader said.
Similarly in south Texas, where thunderstorms have cooled temperatures to below normal levels, prices gained almost 10 cents to the mid-$2.30s.
In west Texas, Permian prices were slightly higher early at $2.30, but buyers quickly disappeared from the market, pushing prices into the low-$2.20s.
"There have been a lot of storage plays in the California markets. Suppliers are long storage," one trader said.
As a result of the ample storage supplies, prices at the southern California border began in the low-$2.40s but eroded into the $2.20s late.

In the Midcontinent, prices failed to rally despite the cold weather now in the region. Forecasts calling for moderating temperatures by the weekend stalled prices in the low-$2.30s, market sources said.
Chicago city-gate values were talked in the high-$2.40s.
In the East, New York city-gate gas prices jumped into the $3.05-3.15 range, up more than 10 cents from Tuesday's levels on prospects for colder weather in the region Thursday.
According to a Reuter poll, natural gas storage levels are expected to show a decline of about 110-125 bcf in this evening's American Gas Association report.
Looking ahead at next month, most traders agree that buyers are still hesitant to step into the March market in anticipation of milder temperatures throughout most of the U.S.
